Home.forAgenciesP1: We're a small development studio in Hungary, inside the EU. Most of our work comes through agencies — the projects they've won but can't staff, the ones needing engineering depth their team doesn't have, or the ones that landed at the wrong time.
Home.forAgenciesP2: We work as your team, not next to it. White-label if you want it, named if you prefer. Your client relationship stays yours.

fourPoints.title: EU-based, EU-billed
fourPoints.body: Hungarian company, EU VAT, invoicing inside the single market. GDPR isn't a checkbox we tick — it's the law we already operate under. No third-country transfer paperwork.

fourPoints.title: Overlapping hours
fourPoints.body: Central European Time. The same working day as our European partners; for US teams, work happens while you sleep and lands before your morning stand-up.

fourPoints.title: Rates that make the maths work
fourPoints.body: Central European rates with Western European engineering standards. For most agencies we cost less than an internal hire — with no recruitment, no onboarding, no bench.

fourPoints.title: One developer, not a rotating pool
fourPoints.body: The same person on your project from start to finish. No handovers, no re-explaining, no account manager relaying half-understood requirements.

web.headline: Sites and stores that are measurably fast
web.p1: The problem with template builds isn't that they're ugly — it's that they're slow, and nobody can tell you why. We build on Next.js, where load speed, search visibility and security are part of the structure rather than a later fix.
web.p2: With a live store, nothing goes offline: we replace pages in phases while the shop keeps trading.
items: Custom design and a reusable design system
Technical SEO: sitemaps, structured data, canonicals
Building on top of an existing backend — WooCommerce, Shopify
Security headers, rate limiting, input validation

access.headline: Some people can't use your site
access.p1: Someone using a screen reader, someone navigating by keyboard, someone with low vision or an unsteady hand — they'd buy too, but often they can't. Not because the site is bad, but because nobody considered them when it was designed.
access.p2: The European Accessibility Act has also extended to consumer-facing online services since 2025. Exactly who it covers is a legal question, and a lawyer answers that — we assess and fix the technical side.
items: Assessment: what blocks use, and how serious it is
Screen reader usability: semantic structure, image descriptions

pulse.headline: One email a month on how the internet sees you
pulse.p1: Most websites get built, and then nobody looks at them again. If it slows down, if a certificate expires, if the contact form breaks — you find out when a customer tells you. Or you don't.
pulse.p2: Pulse watches it for you. Not scores — a letter about what changed and what's worth doing.
items: Load speed: we report the change, not the score
SSL certificate expiry — flagged in advance
Indexing: is the site visible in search
Google profile: new reviews, shifting average
Suggested replies to reviews — you send them
pulse.deviceBelow: Sample. The actual letter is built from your data.

letter.title: August summary
letter.siteLine1: Up all month. Load time 2.1s — that's fine.
letter.siteLine2: ⚠️ Your SSL certificate expires in 24 days. If it isn't renewed, browsers will flag the site as "not secure".
letter.googleLine: 8 new reviews came in. Average moved from 4.7 to 4.8.
letter.watchLine: Two reviews mention it's hard to reach you by phone. If that keeps coming up, a call-back request on the site might help.
letter.actionsLabel: What you can do this month
letter.action1: Renew SSL — we'll handle it if you ask
letter.action2: Update opening hours on the Google profile for the long weekend

pulse.emphasis1: We ask for a review, not a rating. Google prohibits soliciting only positive reviews. We don't: the customer gets a neutral request. If the work is good, the good reviews follow.
pulse.emphasis2: The machine drafts the reply. You send it. We prepare the response, but we never post in your name automatically. One badly judged reply does more damage than ten thank-yous repair.

faq.question: Do you guarantee accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. Compliance is a legal determination and a lawyer makes it. What we guarantee: the technical barriers get assessed, documented and removed, and you get a written record of what changed.

faq.question: Does Pulse fix problems automatically?
faq.answer: No. Pulse detects and reports. Fixing is either a separate instruction or comes out of a monthly retainer — because an automatic change to a live site without anyone looking at it is how outages happen.

faq.question: How is the final price set?
faq.answer: After scoping. We discuss what you need, review the existing systems, then give a fixed price and date — not a range.

faq.question: Can you work white-label?
faq.answer: Yes, and most of our agency work is. Your client relationship stays yours. If you'd rather name us, that's fine too.

Engagement.howWeWorkIntro: We don't publish percentage guarantees, because they either can't be kept or they belong in the contract. Instead, here's how we actually operate.

howWeWorkItems.title: Infrastructure
howWeWorkItems.body: We deploy on Vercel, which provides global CDN and automatic scaling. Availability is covered by the provider's own guarantee — that's theirs to make, not ours.

howWeWorkItems.title: Incident handling
howWeWorkItems.body: Monitoring runs on the systems we operate. For critical failures we respond within hours on working days — the specific response time belongs in the operating agreement, not on a marketing page.

howWeWorkItems.title: Data protection
howWeWorkItems.body: Privacy notice, cookie handling, data processing agreement — part of the project, not an afterthought. Compliance is ongoing work, so we maintain it.

howWeWorkItems.title: Transparency
howWeWorkItems.body: Weekly or fortnightly written reporting on what happened and what's next. If something slips, you hear it in advance — not on the deadline.

faq.question: How is the final price set?
faq.answer: After scoping. We discuss what you need, review the existing systems, then give a fixed price and date — not a range. If scoping shows you need something different from what you asked for, we say so.

faq.question: Is there a minimum commitment?
faq.answer: No. Project work runs per project; retainers are monthly and cancellable on the notice period in the agreement.

faq.question: Can you work white-label?
faq.answer: Yes, and most of our agency work is. Your client relationship stays yours. If you'd rather name us, that's fine too.

faq.question: What if the client needs something you haven't listed?
faq.answer: Ask. If we can't do it well, we'll say so — and often we can point you to someone who can.

faq.question: Who owns the code?
faq.answer: Your client, or you, depending on your arrangement. IP assignment is in the contract from the start. Nothing is locked to us.

Seo.intro: Search has split in two. Google measures the technical foundation; AI search reads structured data, not marketing prose. We build both — and we don't just talk about it.
Seo.proofClosing: Most SEO agencies don't have a sitemap on their own site. Go and look — seriously, open it. If any of ours doesn't work, tell us and we'll fix it.
Seo.changedLeftBody: Load speed, layout stability and response time are ranking factors now, not comfort issues. A slow site doesn't lose because it's ugly — it loses because Google ranks it lower.
Seo.changedRightBody: More people simply ask an AI. These systems don't read keywords, they read structure. If that structure isn't machine-readable, someone else appears in the answer.
Seo.pillarSeoIntro: What Google measures. Server-side rendering means the crawler sees content immediately — no waiting for a browser to assemble it.
pillarSeoItems: Server-side rendering — the crawler reads content immediately
Automatic sitemap and robots.txt — new pages included without anyone remembering
Core Web Vitals — the three metrics Google actually measures
Canonicals and redirects — the most expensive mistake to skip during a migration
Seo.pillarAeoIntro: What language models read. We can't guarantee an AI cites you — nobody can. What we can do is make sure there's something worth citing: clean structure, unambiguous data, machine-readable.
pillarAeoItems: Schema.org and JSON-LD — company data, articles, services, FAQs
Structured FAQs — can appear directly in results, before the click
Unambiguous company data — the same everywhere, no contradictions
Content that answers questions — not keyword stuffing

processSteps.title: 01 · Assessment
processSteps.body: Where you stand: speed, indexing, structure, structured data. You get a list of what's missing — whether or not you continue with us.

processSteps.title: 02 · Build
processSteps.body: Fixing the technical foundation. If the current system can't carry it, a rebuild — but phased, so you don't lose traffic on the way.

processSteps.title: 03 · Maintenance
processSteps.body: Search engines change, and so does your site. If you want operations too, we track it.

faq.question: How long before results show?
faq.answer: Technical fixes appear in indexing within weeks. Ranking movement is slower — three to six months for competitive terms. Anyone promising faster either doesn't understand it or isn't being honest.

faq.question: Do you guarantee first position?
faq.answer: No, and avoid anyone who does. Google decides ranking, not your supplier. What we can guarantee: the technical foundation will be sound, measurable, and verifiable by you.

faq.question: Is AEO actually worth it?
faq.answer: It brings little traffic today, but it's growing fast — and the structured data it requires also helps in conventional Google results. So it isn't wasted spend even if AI search grows slower than expected.

faq.question: Can you improve an existing site, or only build new?
faq.answer: Both. The assessment tells you which is better value — sometimes fixing the current system is cheaper and faster.

faq.question: How do I know you actually did it?
faq.answer: The same way you can check us: sitemap, robots.txt, Rich Results Test, PageSpeed. Public, free tools — you don't have to take our word for it.
